contract:
Static primary scheduling contract, pinned to Meerkat/MobKit 0.8.42.
This packaged reference is source documentation, not an observed destination catalog,
installed schedule, native tool invocation, provider result or restart proof.
The version guard checks the installed Python SDK only. Independently verify the
actual gateway version, granted tools and returned native records on the destination.

Authority and authoring:
- tools.schedule enables the eight meerkat_schedule_* tools for the granted class.
  This family grant is not a per-schedule ownership ACL. Application ownership and
  reconciliation must retain exact native records, IDs and intended configuration.
- The schemas below are extracted from pinned Rust tools.rs, with the actual
  CurrentSessionScheduleToolDispatcher current_session enum injection applied.
  They are declarations of the native tools, not new installer or Python APIs.
- Create requires trigger, target, misfire_policy, overlap_policy and
  missing_target_policy. Optional fields are name, description, labels,
  planning_horizon_days and planning_horizon_occurrences. There is no occurrences
  authoring key, submission idempotency key, revision precondition or desired_definition.
- Update is flat: schedule_id plus whichever CREATE fields change. Only schedule_id
  is required. Do not wrap changes in update, arguments or desired_definition.
  Omitted fields retain their values; successful update increments native revision.
- Get, pause, resume, delete and occurrences each take {"schedule_id":"native UUID"}.
  List takes {}. Retain native ID case/value rather than synthesizing an application ID.
- Pausing prevents future firing but does not cancel already in-flight occurrences.
  Delete tombstones the schedule and is not resumable; occurrence history remains.
  Native service.list() filters deleted schedules despite the catalog description;
  get by a retained ID can retrieve its exact current object. An absent list entry
  alone is not proof that an uncertain create never committed.

Native result JSON (inside the native ToolResult payload):
- Create/get/update/pause/resume/delete return a Schedule object directly.
- List returns {"schedules":[Schedule,...]}; occurrences returns {"occurrences":[Occurrence,...]}.
- Schedule uses schedule_id, phase and revision, NOT id, status or version aliases.
  phase is active, paused or deleted. Retain exact returned native revision.
- Schedule also returns trigger, target, misfire_policy, overlap_policy,
  missing_target_policy, next_occurrence_ordinal, machine_state and optional
  planning_cursor_utc/superseded_ack_ids. Operational machine_state is native-owned.
- ScheduleConfig is flattened into that object: optional name/description, labels
  (omitted if empty), planning_horizon_days, planning_horizon_occurrences,
  created_at_utc, updated_at_utc and optional deleted_at_utc. No nested config wrapper.
- CalendarTriggerSpec serialization emits minute/hour/day_of_month/month/day_of_week,
  using {"kind":"any"} for each omitted field. A missing year remains absent (None);
  do not invent a year constraint. For example, an authored calendar with only
  minute/hour returns day_of_month/month/day_of_week={"kind":"any"} after native get.
  Compare the documented native canonical meaning rather than literal sparse input
  dictionaries. Preserve actual explicit constraints, policies and resolved ownership;
  normalization must not ignore changed configuration or claim destination execution.
- A supplied-looking object from an agent callback is a claim, not an independently
  observed scheduler receipt. Keep claimed records pending until actual native
  tool evidence is bound to the operation and inspected configuration.

Agent-owned continuing targets:
- Author from the responsible member's actual schedule tools using
  {"target_kind":"session","type":"current_session","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"..."}}.
- current_session is a tool-host shortcut, not a persisted TargetBinding variant.
  The ordinary resolver uses resumable_session. The configured mob-member resolver
  uses target_kind=identity, type=resumable_identity and a host-minted
  mob_member:{"schema":"meerkat.schedule.mob_member_identity.v2","mob_id":"...","member":"..."}
  identity, preserving the action. Do not construct that identity by guessing.
- MobKit's compatibility dispatcher can also map a bridged resumable_session prompt
  to target_kind=mob, type=member, mob_id/member_id and action={type:send,content:...}.
  This mapping requires a resolvable mob member and no nonempty session-only
  system_prompt, skill_refs or additional_instructions. Read the actual returned
  target and check its responsible stable member; literal equality to current_session
  input would incorrectly reject an intentional native resolution.
- Advertised authoring target schemas omit host_runnable in this pinned release.
  SDK host_runnables/on_schedule_fire registration is supported independently but
  does not create a definition or permit bypassing authoring schemas.

Delivery and useful work:
- Occurrence phases are pending, claimed, dispatching, awaiting_completion,
  completed, skipped, misfired, superseded or delivery_failed. Occurrence references
  and native delivery identity must come from actual native records, not a nonce.
- MobKit member dispatch may mark scheduled delivery completed at tracked native
  admission and retain work_ref in the receipt. That is not completed agent work,
  a callback outcome, a proposal, message delivery or authorized physical action.
- The gateway mints a per-build callback scope from the native identity, and the
  SDK resolves scope plus tool name independently of model arguments. A genuine
  identity-scoped application callback can validate and persist a domain
  result independently of the later conversational terminal. Its confirmed domain
  result is useful evidence; do not require another agent turn solely to re-confirm
  it. Keep original turn/occurrence correlation unknown when not exposed, and keep
  domain completion, native turn completion and business permission distinct.
- Restart proof requires the real persisted definition/target and observed restored
  delivery plus the requested application's callback/result readback. This static
  reference and offline schema tests establish none of that destination behavior.
- Inspect before create and reconcile interrupted mutations from actual inventory.
  Preserve operation/ID/config/receipt evidence and uncertain state across restart;
  do not blindly create another schedule or modify unrelated ones.
- Timing, timezone, misfire/overlap, cost and notification policy are user/application
  choices. Schema examples and primary-source recommendations are not chosen defaults.

Pinned identity completion observation:
- Separate dispatch admission from wait_for_completion on its returned
  completion_baseline. A later inspect failure does not undo admission and is
  never permission to resend the original work or repeat a schedule mutation.
- In 0.8.42, member-status observation permit exhaustion is wrapped through
  MobError -> BridgeError::Mob -> IdentityRuntimeError::Internal -> JSON-RPC.
  The exact inspect error payload and SDK exception fields are below. Its code
  is -32603 and the data field is omitted (SDK data=None); a nullable data field
  also decodes to SDK None. The bare observation_lane_saturated fixture does
  not represent this wire error. Other errors can share -32603.
- Classify this known category only for a RpcError in the caller's observation
  stage, actual mobkit/inspect_identity method, exact code and complete message.
  Stage is caller context, not an additional native RPC field. Do not split off
  one arbitrary prefix or use marker-substring matching for unrelated errors.
- Retry only the observation on the SAME admitted baseline, with a bounded
  deadline/backoff and cancellation. Missing admission/baseline, changed
  incarnation, unknown/provider errors and schedule mutation ambiguity remain
  separate. Capture safe typed diagnostics without raw error/credential data.
- The exact payload is static primary documentation. It does not diagnose an
  earlier failure whose original code/message/method was discarded, or prove
  actual destination recovery, turn completion or useful domain work.

trigger.description: When the schedule fires. Uses internally tagged JSON with a "type" field. Three types: "once" fires at a single UTC timestamp. "interval" fires repeatedly every N seconds from a start time (optional end_at_utc). "calendar" fires on cron-style fields in a named IANA timezone. Examples: {"type":"once","due_at_utc":"2026-04-10T14:00:00Z"} | {"type":"interval","start_at_utc":"2026-04-10T14:00:00Z","every_seconds":60} | {"type":"calendar","timezone":"UTC","minute":{"kind":"values","values":[0]},"hour":{"kind":"values","values":[9,17]}}.

due_at_utc.description: Deliver once at this UTC timestamp.

end_at_utc.description: Optional final due time in UTC.

timezone.description: IANA timezone such as Europe/Stockholm or UTC.

day_of_week.description: Weekday values using the scheduler's cron-style domain: 0-6 and weekday names such as MON or FRI.

target.description: Where the schedule delivers. Uses target_kind to select session, identity, or mob. Session targets: exact_session (deliver to a known session_id; fails if session is gone), resumable_session (deliver to a session_id that may be idle; runtime resumes it -- best for stable long-lived sessions), materialize_on_demand_session (create a new session on first fire using a "create" spec, then reuse it -- use when no session exists yet). Identity targets: resumable_identity (deliver to the current materialized session for a stable agent identity; host resolves at fire time). The identity string must be a form a schedule host on this surface can resolve, such as the mob-member form minted by the host; free-form strings are refused at create. Mob-member identity targets accept only prompt actions without session-only overrides (no system_prompt, skill_refs, or additional_instructions). Mob targets: member, flow, spawn_helper, fork_helper (deliver to a mob member or flow). Examples: schedule for yourself {"target_kind":"session","type":"current_session","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Check in"}} | mob member {"target_kind":"identity","type":"resumable_identity","identity":"mob_member:{\"schema\":\"meerkat.schedule.mob_member_identity.v2\",\"mob_id\":\"ops\",\"member\":\"watcher\"}","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Check in"}} | {"target_kind":"session","type":"materialize_on_demand_session","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Run report"},"create":{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6"}}.

prompt.description: Either a plain text string or a list of multimodal content blocks.

system_prompt.description: Appended as an ordinary System message at this scheduled turn boundary.

bound_session_id.description: Only used by persisted materialize_on_demand_session schedules after the first materialization.

identity.description: Stable agent identity resolved by the schedule host at occurrence delivery time. Must be a host-recognized form (for example mob_member:{...} as minted by the host); arbitrary strings are refused at create because no host could ever deliver them.

system_prompt.description: Appended as an ordinary System message at this scheduled turn boundary.

params.description: Raw JSON value for mob flow parameters.

content.description: Either a plain text string or a list of multimodal content blocks.

misfire_policy.description: What happens when the scheduler misses an occurrence's due time (e.g., downtime or lag). {"type":"skip"} (recommended): discard overdue occurrences after a ~30s grace window. {"type":"catch_up_within","window_seconds":N}: deliver the occurrence if it is overdue by less than N seconds, otherwise misfire. Use skip unless you specifically need late delivery.

overlap_policy.description: What happens when a new occurrence fires while a previous one is still running. "skip_if_running" (recommended): skip the new occurrence to prevent pile-up. "allow_concurrent": deliver both, allowing parallel execution. Use skip_if_running unless the target is designed for concurrent prompts.

missing_target_policy.description: What happens when the target session or mob does not exist at fire time. "mark_misfired" (recommended): record the occurrence as misfired so failures are visible. "skip": silently skip the occurrence. Use mark_misfired unless you expect transient target absence and do not want noise.

observation_error_contract.scope: Static pinned identity completion-observation error contract, not evidence of a destination failure or authority to replay delivery.

rpc_error.message: internal: inspect: session bridge mob error: mob lifecycle operation admission is still pending at observation_lane_saturated: member_status_observation

message_wrapper_chain: mob lifecycle operation admission is still pending at {stage}: {intent}
observation_error_contract.classification: Require RpcError, caller observation stage, actual method mobkit/inspect_identity, code -32603 and this complete exact message for this pinned category. The bare stage string or an arbitrary marker substring is not the native wire contract. Do not generalize all -32603 or RpcError values as transient.
observation_error_contract.retry_boundary: After a returned admission with its completion_baseline, bounded retry/backoff may repeat wait_for_completion on that same baseline. Never resend the admitted work, authorize a schedule mutation, infer an absent original admission or replace a superseded baseline from this inspect error. Unknown/admission errors remain uncertain and require separate diagnosis. Cancellation and absolute observation deadlines remain effective.
observation_error_contract.diagnostic_boundary: Retain bounded stage, actual RPC method, numeric code, exception class and known category. Do not retain arbitrary raw error message/data/request content/credentials. A local attempted method is not proof that a non-RPC exception came from that RPC.
